one_liner: A tech-enabled grocery retail network for small towns
business_model: A tech-enabled grocery retail network for small towns. It rebrands existing neighbourhood stores under its own name and provides standardised pricing, supply, discounts and digital billing. Founded 2020, operating in small towns of Andhra Pradesh.

claims.text: A tech-enabled grocery retail network for small towns. It rebrands existing neighbourhood stores under its own name and provides standardised pricing, supply, discounts and digital billing. Founded 2020, operating in small towns of Andhra Pradesh.
Risks recorded by the fund: Operationally intense, thin margins, store-owner trust and retention, supply chain in small towns. Limited data on same-store sales growth at the time.

Partner assessment of founders from the meeting: Anil Thontepu and Neeraj Menta. Thontepu came from growth and product work at a Southeast Asian services marketplace; Menta had co-founded a cafeteria-management company and worked in fintech. A complementary pair: one thinks in customer acquisition and product, the other in operations and building a business from nothing. Both were willing to spend months in small-town stores learning how shopkeepers actually operate, which is not the usual profile of a metro-based tech founder. Concern: rural supply-chain execution is tough and neither had run a retail network at scale.
